name: Spell slots
says: A leveled spell is cast by expending a slot of its level or higher; with none left it cannot be cast; slots return on rests.
does: A cast spends the chosen slot (or pact slot) in the same transaction as the effect; a leveled spell with no free slot of its level or above is disabled with NO_SLOT; a resend spends nothing twice; the master may also correct slots by hand (RN-02).
seen: Slot choices with how many are free on the cast sheet; a short word for no slot.
code: backend/internal/rules/combat/turn.go spellReason, slotChoices; backend/internal/play/combat_cast.go castFlow (chosenSlot, spend); backend/internal/play/casting.go castPlan

name: Casting a spell at a higher level
says: A spell cast with a higher-level slot gains the benefit its higher-level text gives (more dice, more targets, more duration or area and so on).
does: Scales what the data holds: damage and healing tables by slot level (at_slot_level), Magic Missile darts and Scorching Ray rays, extra targets per slot level (per_slot_level or the 'additional creature' text pattern), Acid Arrow's later damage, Aid, False Life, Fog Cloud radius; any other higher-level benefit with no data behind it is not applied.
seen: The spell details sheet prints the SRD higher-level text; no reminder on the cast sheet for a benefit the engine does not apply.
code: backend/internal/rules/spelldetails.go DamageAtChoosing; backend/internal/rules/spelltarget.go srdTarget; backend/internal/play/combat_spells.go maxTargetsOf; backend/internal/play/lasting_effects_spells.go defAtSlot; backend/internal/play/zones_cast.go withZoneSize
fix: A note or effect row per spell whose higher-level text has no data, or a generic 'see higher-level text' line on the cast sheet slot picker.

name: Cantrips cost no slot
says: A cantrip is a level 0 spell cast at will with no slot, and every cantrip of a class is always available.
does: Level 0 spells skip the slot check entirely (spellReason only asks for slots when level > 0); cantrips are always in the turn options and cost only the action or bonus action of their casting time.
seen: Cantrips listed first in the options with no slot cost.

name: Cantrip damage by character level
says: A damage cantrip grows at character levels 5, 11 and 17 (dice by total character level, not class level).
does: The damage table keyed by character level (at_character_level) is read with the sheet's total level, multiclass included; Eldritch Blast beams are counted at the same levels.
seen: The cast sheet shows the cantrip's dice from the attack's spell_dice.

name: Ritual casting
says: A spell with the ritual tag can be cast as a ritual, 10 minutes longer, with no slot and never at a higher level, only by a caster whose class has Ritual Casting (bard, cleric, druid and wizard spellbook).
does: Outside a combat the cast takes the casting time plus 10 minutes, spends no slot, refuses a slot sent with a ritual, refuses a spell with no ritual tag (NOT_A_RITUAL) and a class without the feature (CLASS_CANNOT_RITUAL); the Pact of the Chain and Book of Ancient Secrets cases are handled; there is no ritual in a combat.
seen: Refusals say why; the casting panel shows the cast going on.

name: Bonus action spell limit
says: After casting a spell with a bonus action you can cast only a cantrip with a casting time of 1 action that turn (and a bonus action spell cannot follow another spell).
does: The turn keeps two flags (spell_cast, bonus_spell_cast); a cantrip of 1 action counts as neither; the second spell is disabled with BONUS_ACTION_SPELL_LIMIT in either order, also for Quickened Spell; reactions do not count.
seen: A disabled spell row with a sentence naming the spell and the limit.
code: backend/internal/rules/combat/turn.go SpellLimited, IsFreeCantrip; backend/internal/play/combat_cast.go noteSpellCast; backend/internal/play/combat_metamagic.go

name: Casting time of 1 reaction
says: A reaction spell is cast in response to its trigger and costs the reaction.
does: The four SRD reaction spells (Shield, Counterspell, Hellish Rebuke, Feather Fall) are answered in reaction windows that spend the reaction and a slot; on the caster's own turn they are not offered as normal options (Shield only when hit); a muted caster cannot cast the verbal ones.
seen: Reaction windows with the slot choices; 'only outside your turn' or 'only when the trigger happens' on the option row.

name: Casting time of a minute or longer
says: A spell that takes 1 minute or more must be cast over that time with the caster concentrating, and fails (slot not spent) if concentration breaks.
does: In a combat it is disabled (CASTING_TIME_TOO_LONG); outside a combat the cast starts in 'casting' with nothing spent and the caster concentrating, the master confirms the time has passed (slot spent, effect applied), and a broken concentration fails it with no slot spent; the app keeps no clock.
seen: A sentence on the disabled row; the casting panel and the master's 'conclude cast' queue.
code: backend/internal/rules/casting.go IsLongCast; backend/internal/rules/combat/turn.go ReasonTooLong; backend/internal/play/casting.go ConfirmCastTimePassed

name: Spell range
says: A spell reaches a target within its range: Self only the caster, Touch within reach, a distance in feet, with Sight, Unlimited and Special left to the table.
does: For a player on a grid map Self reaches the caster alone, Touch 5 ft and a ranged spell its distance (check by squares between centres, rounded down), before anything is spent; the master is never held to range; sight, unlimited and special ranges and a combat or session without a map are the master's call.
seen: The spell details sheet shows the range; a too-far target is refused with a reason; no reminder for the ranges the engine leaves open.
fix: A short reminder on the cast sheet for a Sight, Unlimited or Special range, and for a combat without a map.

name: Verbal components
says: A caster must be able to speak the words to cast a spell with a verbal component.
does: Only Silence is applied: a creature entirely inside a Silence zone cannot cast a spell with a verbal component, and the verbal reaction spells are refused there; a gagged or otherwise mute caster is not ruled; a verbal spell also gives a hidden caster's position away.
seen: The refusal says the caster cannot speak where it stands; the details sheet lists V.

name: Somatic components
says: A spell with a somatic component needs a free hand with the gestures; a caster can use the hand holding a weapon or shield only if able to.
does: Nothing checks hands, bound hands, restraints or a held shield or weapon when a spell with S is cast; the letter S is data only.
seen: The details sheet lists the component letters (V, S, M) of the spell; no rule text.
fix: A reminder line on the cast sheet for a spell with S when the caster holds two items or is restrained.

name: Material components
says: A spell with a material component needs the listed materials (or a component pouch or a spellcasting focus, unless the material has a cost or is consumed).
does: No inventory is read for materials; the cast never asks for them and never refuses; only Revivify asks the caster to confirm the diamonds before the cast.
seen: The details sheet shows the component line with the material text; a table feature that waives materials says 'no material' with its name.

name: Spellcasting focus and component pouch
says: A component pouch or a spellcasting focus stands in for material components that have no cost; a material with a cost must be provided.
does: Neither the pouch nor a focus is read; nothing distinguishes a material that a focus can replace from one with a cost.
seen: nothing
fix: A reminder line on the details sheet when the material text has a gp cost ('needs the real material, a focus does not replace it').

name: Costly and consumed materials
says: A material with a gold cost must be had to cast, and a spell that says it consumes the material uses it up.
does: Only Revivify's diamonds are handled (a required confirmation that they were spent); no gold, item or inventory is deducted for it or for any other costly material; the others are the table's.
seen: The material text with its price on the details sheet; the Revivify confirmation text.

name: Spell duration
says: A spell lasts for its duration (instantaneous, a time, until dispelled or special) and then ends; it also ends with the end of its concentration.
does: Lasting effects of spells that have an effect row run on rounds and game time (10 rounds a minute) and end on time, concentration, a rest that covers them, or the master; outside a combat a cast record ends with a rest or by the master; a spell with no effect row is only logged and its time is the master's to track.
seen: The effect card shows the rounds left or 'lasts 1 minute'; the log names the spell.
fix: An effect row (condition, modifier or note with text) for each spell with a duration the engine does not time.

name: Concentration: one spell at a time
says: A creature concentrates on only one spell; casting another concentration spell ends the first.
does: Casting a concentration spell replaces the current one, ends its effects, zones and summoned creatures, and the log names the one that ended; the same in a combat and out of one (one concentrating row per caster); readying a spell holds the concentration.
seen: The log line says which concentration ended; a confirmation asks before ending one outside a combat.

name: Concentration: Constitution save on damage
says: When a concentrating creature takes damage it makes a Constitution save, DC 10 or half the damage taken, whichever is higher, once for each source of damage.
does: The DC (max(10, damage/2), one save per source, a spell is one source) is right, but the damage counted is only what temporary hit points did not absorb: damage fully absorbed by temporary hit points opens no save at all and a partly absorbed hit lowers the DC; the SRD says 'damage you take' and does not exclude damage absorbed by temporary hit points (reading of the text; the master can end concentration by hand but cannot ask this save).
seen: The save prompt shows the DC to the master only; nothing says a save was skipped for temporary hit points.
fix: Count the full damage of the hit (before temporary hit points) when working out whether a save opens and its DC.

name: Concentration ends when incapacitated or killed
says: Concentration ends when the caster is incapacitated or dies.
does: At 0 hit points it ends with no save (character, NPC, master's hit point correction); an incapacitating condition that arrives as a lasting effect or a failed-save condition ends it; an incapacitating condition the master sets by hand in the conditions dialog does not end it, the master ends concentration by hand.
seen: The conditions dialog says every other effect of a condition is the master's to apply; the log says when concentration ends.
fix: Call dropConcentrationIfIncapacitated from markConditions/afterConditionsSet, or add the reminder to the dialog row for an incapacitating condition.

name: Concentration: violent environment
says: The master may require a Constitution save (DC 10) to keep concentration when the caster is in a violent environment such as a storm-tossed ship.
does: No such prompt; the master can only ask a plain save or end concentration by hand.
seen: nothing
fix: A master action 'ask a concentration save (DC)' reusing the concentration window.

name: Targets need a clear path
says: A spell that targets a creature needs a clear path to it: total cover blocks it, and a target must be one the caster can see when the spell says so.
does: On a grid map the server refuses a single-target spell on a target behind total cover (a wall, a closed door; creatures and crates do not block), targets are limited to what the player sees (fog), and an area spell may still include a creature behind cover for the master to judge.
seen: Refused with a cover reason; an unseen target is 'not found'.

name: Number of targets
says: A spell affects only the number of targets its text gives (one creature, up to N, any number in an area), plus extra targets at higher slots.
does: Target kind and count come from the data (and spell_targets.json); the server refuses more targets than the spell takes for a player (the master is never held); a spell attack takes one roll per target; a spell with no structured count is read from the SRD text.
seen: The cast sheet shows 'one creature', 'several creatures' or the area and limits the picks; the refusal says the maximum.

name: Areas of effect: cone, cube, cylinder, line, sphere
says: An area spell fills a cone, cube, cylinder, line or sphere from its point of origin; cones and lines start next to the caster, spheres and cylinders are centred on a point, a cube has its origin on a face; the area spreads around corners only where the spell says.
does: On a grid map the caster places the area and the server lists who is inside (square-centre rule, eight directions, caster's own square left out of a cone or line), blocks it behind total cover from the origin and spreads around corners as the spell says; without a map the caster lists the targets and the master judges (RN-25).
seen: A preview of the area and who is inside on the cast sheet; a hint when the area is empty.
code: backend/internal/rules/grid/area.go FromPoint, FromCaster, OpenArea; backend/internal/play/combat_cast.go planPlacedArea

name: Cover and area spells
says: Cover for an area spell is measured from the point of origin and adds +2 or +5 to the Dexterity saving throw only.
does: Cover is worked out from the origin for each target and added to the Dexterity save only; Sacred Flame ignores it; total cover from the origin takes the creature out of the area.
seen: The save sources list the cover bonus.

name: Spell saving throws
says: A target makes the saving throw the spell names against the caster's spell save DC (8 + proficiency + casting ability modifier); success may halve or negate.
does: The DC is 8 + proficiency + ability modifier on the sheet; the server rolls each NPC target's save, a player's save is rolled in the app or typed, whoever passes takes half or nothing as the spell says; Evasion is applied.
seen: The save result in the log; the DC only for the master and the caster's player unless the table shows it.

name: Spell attack rolls
says: A spell attack rolls d20 + proficiency + casting ability modifier against the target's AC, with the usual advantage and disadvantage (a ranged spell attack has disadvantage with a hostile creature within 5 ft), and a 20 is a critical hit.
does: The bonus is proficiency + ability modifier; one d20 per target; advantage and disadvantage from the attack-mode rules (including a hostile creature near a ranged spell attack); critical on 20 or the table's widened range; cover adds to AC; a hit opens pending damage.
seen: The roll sources list each advantage or disadvantage.

name: Combining magical effects
says: The effects of the same spell cast several times do not combine: the most potent applies while their durations overlap, or the most recent if equally potent.
does: A new casting of a spell on a target always ends the older one and keeps the newer, with no comparison of potency, so a weaker later casting (a smaller bonus, a lower-slot Acid Arrow) replaces a stronger one; only Aid and False Life keep the stronger value (the master can end and re-add the stronger effect by hand).
seen: The log says the older effect ended as replaced.
fix: Compare the potency of the two castings in dropSameSpell and keep the stronger one (the later if equal) for the effects that scale.

name: No spellcasting in armor without proficiency
says: A creature wearing armor it is not proficient with cannot cast spells (and has disadvantage on Strength and Dexterity checks, saves and attack rolls).
does: A character in armor or a shield it is not proficient with casts nothing: every spell is disabled (ARMOR_NOT_PROFICIENT), also reaction spells and spell attacks, in a combat and out of one, for the master too; NPCs, creatures and beast forms are not held.
seen: A sentence on each disabled spell and a sheet warning.

name: Bright light
says: In bright light creatures see normally; light sources shed bright light out to a radius.
does: On a map with fog a square is bright when the base light, painted light or a light source's bright radius reaches it by a clear line; torch, lamp, lantern, candle, Light and Daylight have their SRD radii as presets the master or a carried light uses; spells that make light do not place one by themselves; on a map without fog nothing is computed.
seen: The fog map shows the square in full colour; presets list the radii.

name: Dim light and lightly obscured areas
says: Dim light makes an area lightly obscured: disadvantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight.
does: Seen in dim light (or in grey) the passive trap check is lowered by 5 and an active Perception trap search rolls with disadvantage (two dice); no other Perception check (a scene check, a puzzle hint) is touched.
seen: The trap notice list shows the penalty for dim light; no other screen says it.
code: backend/internal/rules/vision/vision.go PassivePenalty; backend/internal/maps/traps_play.go penaltyAt; backend/internal/play/traps_search.go rollSearchWithMode
fix: A reminder on the scene check dialog when the checking character stands in dim light on a fog map.

name: Darkness (heavily obscured)
says: In darkness a creature without special senses is effectively blind there: the area is heavily obscured.
does: On a fog map a dark square is unseen to a player without darkvision, blindsight, truesight or Devil's Sight in range; attack rolls by a player at an NPC the player cannot see have disadvantage and no reactions come from creatures that cannot see the mover; an NPC attacking a player in the dark, anyone on a map without fog, and the blinded effects on the creature itself are not ruled.
seen: The master gets a warning for each player character that sees nothing where it stands; the map greys what is seen only by darkvision.
code: backend/internal/rules/vision/vision.go InTheDark; backend/internal/play/combat_advantage.go unseen; backend/internal/play/combat_fog.go reactorSees
fix: A reminder on the NPC attack card when its target stands in the dark.

name: Heavily obscured areas (fog, foliage)
says: In a heavily obscured area (Fog Cloud, Stinking Cloud, dense foliage) a creature is effectively blind, and a creature cannot see into it.
does: Only Fog Cloud, Stinking Cloud and Wall of Fire zones block the line of sight on a fog map and nothing is seen from inside but the viewer's own square; blindsight sees through within range and truesight does not (the table's reading); foliage or other heavily obscured terrain is not a layer; RN-37 says a cloud gives no advantage or disadvantage to an attack, yet a player's attack at an NPC the fog hides still gets the unseen-target disadvantage.
seen: The zone card for the master; the map hides the covered squares from players.
fix: A heavily obscured terrain layer, and a note on the zone card about the blinded effect.

name: Darkvision
says: Within its range darkvision sees dim light as bright and darkness as dim light, in shades of grey only.
does: Within range a dim square is bright and a dark one grey (lightly obscured, so -5 passive), beyond range nothing; it fails in magical darkness; the range comes from the race, a feature, an effect or a creature's stat block.
seen: Grey shading on the map; the sheet shows the sense and range.

name: Blindsight
says: With blindsight a creature perceives its surroundings within its range without relying on sight.
does: Within range it sees any square regardless of light, in grey, even in magical darkness and through a cloud; it takes no light penalty on passive checks within range.
seen: Grey shading on the map; the sheet shows the sense and range.

name: Truesight
says: Truesight sees in normal and magical darkness, sees invisible creatures and through illusions and shapechanges, and into the Ethereal Plane, within its range.
does: Only the darkness part is applied: within range every square is bright, magical darkness included; invisible creatures, illusions, true forms and the Ethereal Plane are not (an invisible target still gives disadvantage to the attacker), and a cloud still blocks it.
seen: The sheet shows the sense and range only.
fix: A sense note on the sheet and the attack card ('truesight: sees invisible creatures within range').

name: Light sources
says: A light source sheds bright light in a radius and dim light for an additional distance (torch 20 and 20, lamp 15 and 30, hooded lantern 30 and 30, candle 5 and 5, Light 20 and 20, Daylight 60 and 60).
does: The master paints or places Luz points and characters carry lights from presets with exactly those radii; the Light, Daylight, Continual Flame and Dancing Lights spells have no effect row and put no light on the map by themselves.
seen: Light presets with radii in metres.

name: Falling damage
says: A fall deals 1d6 bludgeoning damage per 10 feet fallen, up to 20d6.
does: Only the pit trap presets fall: a simple pit of 10 ft deals 1d6 and a hidden pit of 20 ft deals 2d6 to the creatures caught, with Feather Fall and Slow Fall windows; any other fall (a cliff, a ledge, a push) has no calculation and is the master's by hand; no 20d6 cap or per-10-ft rule exists in code.
seen: The pit preset says its depth and dice; nothing for other falls.
fix: A master action 'fall N ft' that rolls Nd6 (N = feet / 10, max 20) bludgeoning and offers Feather Fall and Slow Fall, plus prone.

name: Landing prone from a fall
says: A creature lands prone from a fall unless it avoids taking damage from the fall.
does: A pit trap gives the prone condition when it fires, even when Feather Fall takes the fall damage away (the creature should land on its feet) or Slow Fall reduces it to 0; the master can remove it by hand in the conditions dialog.
seen: The log shows the prone condition given by the trap.
fix: Remove the trap's prone condition from a creature whose fall damage a Feather Fall discarded or a Slow Fall brought to 0.

name: Holding your breath
says: A creature can hold its breath for 1 + its Constitution modifier minutes (minimum 30 seconds).
does: No air or breath count exists; only an effect or table feature 'breathes water' is a sheet note; the master keeps the time.
seen: Only the table-content editor hint for the breathes-water effect, which says the game keeps no breath or drowning count.
code: backend/internal/rules/tablemenu.go (breathes_water); no air count anywhere in backend/internal or web/src/app
fix: A master timer 'holding breath' with the Constitution-based duration.

name: Suffocating and drowning
says: A creature out of breath survives a number of rounds equal to its Constitution modifier (minimum 1), then drops to 0 hit points and is dying and cannot regain hit points until it breathes.
does: No suffocation count, no drop to 0 hit points and no block on healing is applied; the master adjusts hit points by hand.
seen: Only the table-content editor hint for the breathes-water effect, which says the game keeps no breath or drowning count.
code: backend/internal/rules/tablemenu.go (breathes_water); backend/internal/play/combat_hit_points.go AdjustCombatantHitPoints (the master corrects hit points by hand)
fix: A master action 'start suffocating' with the rounds from the Constitution modifier and the drop to 0 hit points at the end.

name: Food and water
says: A character needs 1 pound of food and 1 gallon of water a day (half with half rations or half water), and going without brings exhaustion after a number of days or a Constitution save.
does: Nothing tracks food, water, days without or the saves; only the long rest dialog has a switch 'without food or drink' that skips the exhaustion recovery.
seen: The long rest dialog hint about food and drink; nothing about daily needs.
fix: A reminder line in the rest card about daily food and water and the exhaustion that follows.

name: Long jump
says: A long jump covers up to the Strength score in feet with a 10 ft running start on foot, half that standing; each foot cleared costs a foot of movement.
does: A player long jump is limited to Strength in feet with a running start (a move of at least 10 ft on foot just before, this turn) and half without, costs its length in movement, passes over difficult terrain and creatures but not walls or a creature at the landing, and Second-Story Work and Step of the Wind change it; it exists only in a combat on a map.
seen: The jump length and the limit in the move panel; too far is refused with the limit.

name: High jump
says: A high jump rises 3 feet + the Strength modifier with a 10 ft running start on foot, half standing; each foot costs a foot of movement.
does: The height is 3 + the Strength modifier (never below 0) running and half standing; the feet are spent from movement and nobody changes square.
seen: The height asked and the limit.

name: Landing a jump in difficult terrain
says: Landing in difficult terrain needs a DC 10 Dexterity (Acrobatics) check or the creature lands prone.
does: The app rolls nothing; the combat log for the master says the jump landed in difficult terrain and tells the Acrobatics DC 10 or prone call.
seen: A line in the master's log only ('jumped ... landed in difficult terrain ... Acrobatics DC 10 or falls prone').

name: Clearing a low obstacle
says: To clear a low obstacle no taller than a quarter of the jump's distance needs a DC 10 Strength (Athletics) check or the jumper hits it.
does: A long jump ignores obstacles on the line except walls and an occupied landing; no check is asked.
seen: nothing
fix: A note on the jump confirmation 'low obstacle: Athletics DC 10'.

name: Travel pace
says: Travel pace is fast, normal or slow (about 4, 3 and 2 miles an hour; 30, 24 and 18 miles a day), with a -5 passive Perception at a fast pace and stealth only at a slow one, and a forced march after 8 hours.
does: The app has no travel pace, distance per hour or forced march rule.
seen: nothing
code: no code found (searched backend/internal and web/src/app)
fix: A reference card of the pace table on the session screen.
